# Fermionic Configuration Limits

This repository studies how fixed local energy accuracy constrains the number
of terms in global fermionic Gaussian expansions. The full scientific account
is organized by topic under science/.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: scientific question, exact headline bounds, reading route,
  reproduction commands, scope and purpose/contact.
- science/README.md: connected physical account and the two proof routes.
- science/model.md: CAR conventions; explicit number-conserving two-body
  Hamiltonian; complete block spectrum; H0 >= Dm; exact preparation and costs.
- science/gaussian_rank.md: exact/border-rank definitions; uniform unnormalized
  approximation input; subset conditioning; positive heat kernel; Jensen and
  Chernoff optimization; all endpoints; stronger inherited asymptotic input.
- science/orthogonal_configurations.md: orthonormal Gaussian-span theorem,
  arbitrary orbital optimization, exact best-determinant energy and the
  subexponential orthogonal configuration energy floor.
- science/perturbations.md: norm-perturbation transfer, equal energy accuracy,
  connected noncommuting hopping family and explicit constant example.
- science/local_certification.md: trusted local measurement, exact one-sided
  sample count, pure-state certificate, closed-convex-hull mixed-state
  guarantee, covariance counterexample and full-copy resource accounting.
- science/algorithmic_scope.md: QSCI/SQD/nonorthogonal-CI output contracts,
  explicit versus implicit expansion, matched accuracy, charged resources,
  and compact product/geminal/cluster/tensor-network alternatives.
- references/README.md: canonical short citation keys.
- references/related_work.md: exact primary-source comparisons and versions,
  inherited ingredients, consequence proved here, and comparison boundaries.
- references/bibliography.bib: reusable primary bibliography.
- verification/README.md: documented scientific checks and their limits.
- verification/checks.py: executable finite algebraic/numerical checks.
- verification/results.json: actual recorded results, distinct from a new run.
- learning/MCARDLE_BRIDGE.md: the selected McArdle et al. (2020) educational
  anchor, verified section/page/equation locators, translated notation,
  worked examples and the missing project-specific reasoning.
- learning/MILESTONES.md: exactly 30 common project-intrinsic milestones;
  M01-M12 background/preliminaries and M13-M30 narrative/innovation,
  with local-to-global synthesis at the end of each phase.

Reader routes:
- Story: science/README.md, model.md, algorithmic_scope.md.
- General-rank theorem: model.md, gaussian_rank.md, then its cited inputs.
- Orbital/configuration optimization: orthogonal_configurations.md.
- Connected physical example: model.md, perturbations.md.
- Measurement and statistics: local_certification.md.
- Attribution: references/related_work.md and bibliography.bib.
- Reproduction: verification/README.md, then its documented commands.
- Learning: learning/MCARDLE_BRIDGE.md and learning/MILESTONES.md, following
  their source pointers into the canonical science pages.

Preserve these distinctions when explaining or editing:
- K counts global Gaussian terms, not arbitrary vector-space dimension,
  raw quantum shots, matrix entries, or every algorithm's runtime.
- Gaussian functions used as chemistry orbital basis functions are not the
  same concept as fermionic Gaussian many-body states. The McArdle review
  supplies the educational vocabulary; the later fidelity/rank papers are
  separate research inputs, and the energy-density lift is proved here.
- A linear CI expansion and an exponential coupled-cluster parametrization
  have different resource counts. The explicit product has a compact doubles
  cluster description even when its Gaussian expansion is exponential.
- The half-energy threshold requires an orthonormal Gaussian basis. General
  nonorthogonal rank and border rank use their smaller certified threshold.
- R = 27(8+2sqrt(7))/256 is the explicit imported rank base. The energy-density
  lift proved here gives q = 1-1/R. The improved rank base 343/243
  is inherited from Wei et al., with an unspecified absolute prefactor.
- Every exponential-rate formula has its stated energy range. Do not extend
  binary relative entropy beyond the permitted Chernoff parameter regime.
- Energies are per four-mode block; divide by four for energy per mode.
- Two-body fermionic interactions can involve four modes. No two-qubit
  locality statement is implied.
- The ground state is easy to prepare and has compact classical product,
  geminal, cluster and tensor-network descriptions. No general hardness or
  quantum advantage is proved.
- The connected perturbation comparison certifies an energy-accurate trial.
  It does not prove a perturbed gap, high fidelity or easy exact preparation.
- The local sample count assumes independent identical copies and trusted
  measurements. Preparing each full copy of the explicit product source
  costs O(m) gates.
- The mixed-state result excludes a precisely defined convex hull; it is
  not a claim about ordinary density-matrix rank or every decomposition term.
- Finite checks validate conventions and examples, not universal asymptotic
  theorems, priority, peer review, or future hosted rendering.
